name: Slider (Multi-Thumb)
description: An extension of the slider with two or more thumbs on a single rail, where each thumb controls one value such as a price range.

keyboard_interactions.action: Increases focused thumb's value by one step
Increases focused thumb's value by one step
Decreases focused thumb's value by one step
Decreases focused thumb's value by one step
Sets focused thumb to its minimum
Sets focused thumb to its maximum
Moves focus between thumbs; tab order stays constant regardless of value

required_attributes.description: Minimum; updated dynamically when dependent on another thumb
Maximum; updated dynamically when dependent on another thumb
Unique accessible name for each thumb

optional_attributes.description: vertical if vertical; default is horizontal

notes: There is no native multi-thumb slider. Two overlaid <input type='range'> elements keep native keyboard support, native value announcement, and native form values — it is almost always better than a div implementation.
Each thumb is its own slider role with its OWN accessible name. 'Price' twice is useless: use 'Minimum price' and 'Maximum price'.

Constrain the thumbs: the min thumb's aria-valuemax is the max thumb's current value, and vice versa. Update them as the values change, or a screen reader announces a range the user cannot actually reach.
Decide and document what happens when thumbs meet — swap, or block. Blocking is easier to understand and easier to announce.
Always provide number inputs alongside for exact entry. It is the single-point alternative (RAWeb 13.10.2), it is far easier for everyone, and it costs almost nothing.
native_element: none — two <input type="range"> overlaid is the most accessible approach available

raweb_criteria.reason: Each thumb is a separate slider and needs its own value and its own accessible name ('Minimum price', 'Maximum price').
Each thumb must be independently keyboard operable.
Each thumb needs its own label — 'Price' alone does not say which end.
Both thumbs need visible focus indicators.
Test 13.10.2 — as with a single slider, dragging is path-based and needs a single-point alternative.
